Where the Papers Are

The deed, statements, policies and beneficiary forms behind Dad's list, on one page.

Download PDF

The deed is in the safe-deposit box, or it was. The beneficiary forms were filled in when Dad opened the accounts, and they've sat in a file ever since.

This page doesn't ask you to read or understand any of them. It asks where each paper is, what date is on it, who holds it, and which ones nobody has seen.

What to findWhere it isIts dateWho holds it
The deed to Dad's home
Deeds to any other real estate
A recent statement for each bank account
A recent statement for each investment account
A recent statement for each retirement account
Insurance policies, with the latest statement for each
Annuity contracts, with the latest statement for each
Beneficiary forms for the retirement accounts, insurance and annuities
Trust papers, if Dad has a trust
Papers for anything owned jointly with someone else
Vehicle titles, and papers for any business interest
The family's list of what Dad owns

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

What nobody has seen, and who will look for it

Anything above with an empty line. Put a name next to each. There's no hurry; a paper nobody has seen is one line on this list.

For example Nobody has seen the beneficiary form for the retirement account. Dad will ask the company for a copy of what's on file.

How to use it

  • Write the date printed on each paper. If it has no date, write “undated.”
  • Don't copy account numbers or summarize a document here. Just say where it is.
  • When something changes, such as an account opened or closed or a beneficiary form updated, change the row and its date.
  • Bring this page with you when you talk with your Medicaid planner or an elder law attorney.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't explain what any deed, statement, policy or form means, or how anything on it would be treated. If you read something you don't understand, that's a question for the company that issued it, for your Medicaid planner or for an elder law attorney. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.
